notes.drag: carriage drag: none until a source gives one
notes.power: one hit destroys a fighter (inferred, as the AIM-9M)
notes.blast_m: the lethal radius is open; held by blast scaling (inferred): the AIM-9A / B's 9 m (ds-aim9) for its 4.5 kg warhead (docs/real-weapons.md §1.4) times the cube root of this warhead's mass ratio (39 kg)
notes.mach: the low end of Mach 4.5–5.8, which the article marks "citation needed"
notes.g_limit: open (the article's "below 5 g" is the launcher's limit at launch)
notes.motion._absAcceleration: 120 m/s², the AIM-9M record's (inferred: no burn time published)
notes.motion._spiralAccelBeta: top speed a / beta: 120 / the top speed
notes.motion.burn: the burn with which the motion flies the published range from 250 m/s before its flight ends 6 s after the burn (missile.rs real_burn, the rule real_weapons.gd gives the AIM-9M)
notes.motion._timeAcceleration: the burn, so the original's reading of the section flies as long
notes.motion._timeConstOrientation: flies straight 0.5 s after launch (the AIM-9M record's)
notes.motion._decoyReject: 0.5 (inferred): a semi-active seeker of 1987 on the launcher's illumination; its Doppler rejection taken lower than the AIM-120's 0.8 (w-chaff; docs/real-weapons.md 2.3)
notes.motion._motorThrust: fitted: the steady thrust with which it reaches its published Mach 4.5 from Mach 0.9 12,000 m up (the Python 5's rule, docs/real-weapons.md §2.1)
notes.motion._propellantKg: inferred: the AIM-9M's share of the launch mass (32 %)
notes.motion._diameterM: the body's diameter, the drag's reference
notes.motion._maxTime: fitted: the straight shot head on, both jets at Mach 0.9 12,000 m up, reaches its published 73 km (the AIM-120's rule, docs/real-weapons.md §2.1)
